memory_candidates.content: bash's `read` (any form, including `IFS=$'\x1f' read`) is fundamentally line-oriented: it stops consuming input at the first real newline regardless of IFS, silently truncating any field containing embedded newlines and blanking every subsequent field in that record. Use `mapfile -d $'\x1f' -t arr <<< "$data"` instead when splitting a record on a custom delimiter where any field might contain embedded newlines -- `mapfile -d` uses the given character as the record terminator instead of newline. Separately, `IFS=<char> read` collapses CONSECUTIVE occurrences of the delimiter (silently dropping empty fields) whenever that character is in bash's IFS-whitespace class (space/tab/newline) -- use a non-whitespace delimiter like the ASCII Unit Separator (0x1f) to avoid this.

When eliminating a per-item subprocess-spawn storm (e.g. N jq calls per loop iteration), encoding each extracted FIELD separately with @base64 and decoding each with its own subprocess call does not remove the spawn-count cost -- it only trades one subprocess type for another (jq spawns become base64 spawns) of the same order of magnitude. Instead, join all fields for one record with a safe delimiter FIRST, then base64-encode the WHOLE joined record ONCE, so decode is a single subprocess spawn per record rather than one per field.

In this repo, `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` (the non-interactive .claude/ redeploy mechanism) has exactly one sanctioned automated caller: skill-orchestrate's Stage MT-3 step 7 inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint, documented in context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md's Automated Exception subsection. Any other agent (including a general-implementation-agent /implement dispatch) must NOT invoke it directly, even when a plan explicitly directs a Phase 5-style redeploy-and-verify step -- the correct response is to verify everything possible via an isolated throwaway root (matching the existing test-suite convention) and record the actual redeploy as a documented Reasoned Exclusion, deferring to a human-invoked interactive Load Core sync.
